Nothing has been decided yet.
So my guess is right! Shall I write the article?
Go ahead and write it. Write it if you are so sure.
You got rejected!
Reporter Kang, why are you doing this to me, seriously?
All you have to do is tell me who it is.
Hold on, we are still coordinating.
Filming is one week away, so how long am I supposed to wait?
You will contact me alone with an exclusive before the day ends, right?

meanings.note: Expresses sudden realization, surprise, or hesitation.

examples.trans: Ah, yes.
Oh, I see!

meanings.note: Used when repeating an action.

examples.trans: See you again!
It is raining again.

meanings.note: Interrogative adverb.

examples.trans: Why are you running?
Why were you late today?

meanings.en: to come (of a feeling, state, or weather)
meanings.note: Used in expressions like 혼란이 오다 (confusion comes) or 비가 오다 (rain falls)

examples.text: 한국에 온 지 일 년 됐어요.
examples.trans: It's been one year since I came to Korea.
I suddenly started feeling sleepy.
Come on, nice to meet you!
Come on, I understand now.
I want to did you sulk right now.
How about trying to did you sulk together tomorrow?
Did you hear about this new?
I was busy today because of new.

meanings.note: loanword from English 'member', commonly used for regular cast members of variety shows or teams

examples.trans: A new member joined.
All our team members gathered.

meanings.note: interrogative pronoun; becomes 누가 before subject particle -가
indefinite pronoun

examples.trans: Did someone come outside?
Who is that person?

meanings.note: Used mostly in negative sentences.

examples.trans: He hasn't come yet.
I still don't know.

meanings.note: Pairs with 나다 (결정 나다, 'a decision is reached') or 하다 (결정하다, 'to decide').

examples.trans: A decision hasn't been reached yet.
I have to make an important decision.

meanings.note: Short-form negation placed directly before verbs and adjectives

examples.trans: I'm not going to the office today.
I haven't watched that movie yet.

meanings.note: Takes a complement marked with 이/가.

examples.trans: I want to become a doctor.
It has already become 12 o'clock.

맞다.gloss: to be right, to be correct

meanings.note: Used to confirm facts or answers.

meanings.en: to fit, to suit, to match
meanings.note: E.g., 사이즈가 맞다 ('the size fits').

examples.trans: Yes, that's my phone number.
These shoes fit my feet perfectly.

meanings.note: Plain first-person singular pronoun used with friends, younger people, or subordinates; contracts to 난 with -는 and becomes 내가 before -가.

examples.trans: I'm going to stay home today.
I'll go first.

meanings.note: Irregular ㅡ-stem verb: 쓰다 + -어 becomes 써.
Commonly used for tools, money, or time.

examples.trans: I write in my diary every night.
I wrote my name on the very first page of the book.
Did you hear about this certainty?
I was busy today because of certainty.

meanings.en: to hold, to carry in one's hand
meanings.note: ㄹ-irregular verb; 들고 가다 means 'to carry along'.

examples.trans: Please take your bag with you.
If it's heavy, I'll carry it.
I want to got turned down! right now.
How about trying to got turned down! together tomorrow?

meanings.note: A person who gathers and reports news.

examples.trans: My dream is to become a reporter.
The reporters asked many questions.

이러다.gloss: to do this, to act like this

meanings.en: to do this, to act like this
meanings.note: Contracted from 이러하다.

examples.trans: Why are you acting like this?
Please don't do this.

meanings.note: Everyday spoken intensifier; can also function as a noun meaning 'the real thing'.

examples.trans: I'm really busy today.
Is that really delicious?
I want to if you let me know right now.
How about trying to if you let me know together tomorrow?

있다.gloss: to exist, to have, to stay

meanings.en: to exist, to be (in a place)
meanings.note: Opposite of 없다.
Marks the possessed item with 이/가.

examples.trans: Do you have time?
Nobody is at home.

related.gloss: to not exist, to not have

보다.gloss: to see, to watch; to take (an exam)

meanings.en: to see, to look at, to watch
meanings.note: Primary meaning.
Idiomatic in 시험을 보다.

examples.trans: I watched a movie on the weekend.
I took the driver's license exam.
Did you hear about this coordination?
I was busy today because of coordination.

meanings.note: Bound noun placed after another noun to indicate an ongoing activity or time period, usually followed by 에 (중에). RR: jung.

examples.trans: I am in a meeting right now.
Please do not make phone calls during class.
Did you hear about this filming too?
I was busy today because of filming too.
Did you hear about this only one week?
I was busy today because of only one week.

meanings.note: verb to remain

examples.trans: Money is left.
Time is left.

meanings.note: interrogative noun asking about time; combines with particles like -부터 (from)

examples.trans: When did you come to Korea?
Since when have you worked here?
I want to wait right now.
How about trying to wait together tomorrow?

meanings.note: The present day; often used adverbially without a particle.

examples.trans: The weather is nice today.
What day of the week is it today?
Did you hear about this exclusively?
I was busy today because of exclusively.

meanings.note: Used in 연락을 하다 ('to contact') and humble 연락을 드리다.

examples.trans: I will contact you later.
I heard from my friend today.

meanings.note: Used for giving things to someone of equal or lower status.

examples.trans: I gave a gift.
Please give me some water.

meanings.note: Bound noun often contracted to 거 in everyday speech.

examples.trans: This is my bag.
Because I think I'm late.

meanings.note: Used for time or order.

examples.trans: Let's meet next time.
The next station is Seoul Station.

meanings.note: Action of coming together with someone.

examples.trans: I meet a friend.
Let's meet tomorrow.
